feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It is generally well written, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and opportunities to sharpen impact through clearer outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and scope over time.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Positioning is focused and modern, especially around digital governance, analytics, Drupal, multimedia, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Header, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; several themes/tools appear multiple times, which weakens punch and wastes space.  
- Add more outcome-oriented results beyond scope metrics: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, adoption improvements, campaign performance, or cost/time savings.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation/hyphenation varies (“organization-wide,” “front-end,” “public-facing” are fine, but list formatting is uneven). No major misspellings found; grammar is strong overall.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience sections. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading” or “delivering.”
- Add a concrete scope marker from recent experience to increase impact, e.g. “10,000+ page websites,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Trim the service list so it feels less like the competencies section; prioritize 3–4 strongest areas.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers scalable digital platforms, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations, including 10,000+ page web ecosystems serving millions of annual users.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- The long capability list duplicates the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize strategic capability areas rather than repeating detailed skill phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, cleaner labels: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “operations” vs. “experiences”; keep all items as parallel noun phrases.
- Consider replacing “Enterprise website modernization” with “Enterprise web modernization” for brevity and consistency with the header/work experience.
- If space is tight, reduce to 6–7 items by combining related areas, e.g., merge multimedia/livestream with multi-channel communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” and several other items repeat language already used in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the subtitle and Topline Skills.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce the CV’s themes, but the block is too dense and repeats several points already covered in Work Experience. It will land better with tighter formatting, parallel phrasing, and clearer emphasis on outcomes or scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add bullets and keep each project to one crisp line with parallel verbs: “Designed…,” “Built…,” “Developed…,” “Launched…”
- Tighten wording: change “AI-enabled”/“AI chat” repetition, and use “10 x 20-foot” for style consistency.
- Emphasize distinguishing details not already stated elsewhere, e.g., “bill-level chat,” “interactive conference display,” “modular campaign architecture.”
- Consider retitling “Recent Projects” to “Selected Recent Projects” for a more polished CV tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- If space is tight, keep only the most distinctive projects here and avoid repeating Drupal, campaign, and video details already covered above.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground 2–3 highest-impact contributions, especially anything measurable or clearly enterprise-level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: “Lead,” “Built,” “Designed,” “Established,” “Improved.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into outcome-led points, e.g.:
- Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve cross-channel communications operations.
- Designed Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Led AI-enabled search development, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX.
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages/users, reduction in publishing time, campaign engagement, search performance, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating Drupal/CMS/front-end details already covered in Topline Skills and Recent Projects.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization overlaps with NACo role; emphasize what is new here: consulting scope, AI search, and campaign builds.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management, leading enterprise modernization and audience growth.”
- Prioritize the website migration as the lead bullet and make impact explicit: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel bullet and add measurable results if available: open/click rates, list growth, follower growth, engagement, video output, event reach, or cost savings.
- Combine operations bullets for concision: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio and expanded analytics/reporting across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, supported by stronger governance, publishing standards, and cross-team planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program growth also appears in prior NACo roles; emphasize the studio build and organizational capability instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership and channel growth, with sharper outcomes and less generic “helped improve” phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets and use stronger verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague support language with concrete operational outcomes: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and coordination.” If possible, add metrics such as send volume, open rates, production cadence, or turnaround time.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive value rather than repeating generic communications phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel” for “Cross-channel” and “Audience-focused” for “Audience strategy” to sound more senior and concise.
- If space allows, add one higher-impact qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “enterprise web modernization” or “AI-informed content discovery,” instead of broad “messaging.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and delivery rather than listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older items unless job-relevant; keep Drupal first, and consider removing jQuery to avoid dating the profile.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization for large public-facing sites” to echo recent 10,000+ page migration work.
- Keep platform names selective; include WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if required by target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; Topline Skills should stay strategic and condensed.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep wording distinct or remove here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making value, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity for KPI design, executive reporting, user-behavior analysis and performance optimization.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive reporting” or “decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider changing “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and content performance analysis” if accurate; it better reflects Clarity + analytics usage.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, such as “analytics infrastructure for 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list in multiple sections; keep Topline Skills more strategic and Technical + IT more exhaustive.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and the in-house studio/event leadership angle.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad task phrasing with capability + scope: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio systems.”
- Reorder by strategic value and recency: lead with studio/event production, then livestreaming, then editing.
- Consider a tighter version: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale language in experience bullets instead of here (e.g., recurring advocacy programming, in-house studio build, event support volume).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid and virtual event production” are partially covered by NACo experience bullets, so keep this skills line concise rather than descriptive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level/relevance, e.g. “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, prioritize strongest/current platforms first: “Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Consider adding version/scope only where meaningful and recent, e.g. “Drupal 10” if tied to current consulting/project work.
- Keep this as a pure platform list; save broader phrases like “CMS modernization” for Topline Skills or experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution”; consider merging or removing one of the two sections.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise/public-sector focus unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more implementation-focused and trim older/basic terms unless they support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: JavaScript/jQuery • HTML/CSS • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows
- Consider replacing “HTML5” and “CSS3” with “HTML/CSS” for concision; version labels add little value at this level.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g., “Drupal front-end implementation,” “serverless scripting,” or “deployment automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one version shorter or more strategic.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere, so avoid adding broad automation language here unless it is specifically technical (e.g., CI/CD, serverless).

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems
- Group by function for clarity and seniority: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show application, not just familiarity: “Used to build content operations, approvals, task routing and cross-team coordination workflows.”
- Consider trimming lower-value tools if space is tight; keep the strongest/recent ones first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are project management tools, so this section should signal workflow design, not just app familiarity.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength from recent roles: enterprise email operations and member communications. It should signal scale and platform ownership, not just list software.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise newsletter operations • Audience segmentation
- If accurate, strengthen further with function-based phrasing: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign deployment • List management • Segmentation • Journey automation
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; lead with the most current/enterprise tool.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Engagement” is vague and overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations”; use more specific email/CRM language.
- Avoid adding analytics terms here, since those are already covered well in “Data, Analytics & Optimization.”

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show depth beyond platform names. Tighten it into a sharper technical stack and replace generic terms with more specific capabilities.

Suggested edit
- Revise to: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • SEO analysis • Experimentation reporting
- Replace “A/B testing” with “Experimentation reporting” unless you directly ran tests; it’s more credible given the experience bullets.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with named outputs or methods, e.g., “Executive dashboards” or “KPI reporting,” if space allows.
- If accurate, consider adding “KPI design” here and removing a less distinctive item like “SEO,” since KPI/reporting is better supported by recent leadership work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Keep one more strategic and the other purely tool-based.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in recent NACo experience, so avoid repeating broad terms here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup for later NACo roles. Tighten it around foundational impact, team-building, and concrete outputs without repeating responsibilities already covered in 2018–2024 roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Make contributions more concrete: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand member-facing communications.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics or scale if available: add event count, video cadence, audience reach, or production volume.
- Clarify supervision scope: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or omit if informal.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with later NACo bullets on governance/publishing systems; keep this at a more foundational level.
- Weekly video updates are also mentioned in the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or early production, not scaling.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles at NACo.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program work; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific verb and deliverable: “Produced multimedia and digital content supporting organizational programs and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-team partners, or types of research/projects supported.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles since it is older and less senior.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later entries already show progression into digital leadership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software, workflows, and production capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so tighten it to tool-specific skills and keep higher-level production strengths elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Creative & Audio/Video Tools”
- Replace with a cleaner, tool-led list: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- If you want one capability line, make it concise and specific: “Video editing • Audio editing • Graphic asset creation”
